topic.original: Should frontier AI labs be legally required to publish full model weights for independent safety audit?
topic.final: Should frontier AI labs be legally required to publish full model weights for independent safety audit?

scope.core_proposition: Whether frontier AI laboratories should be legally mandated to release complete model weights so independent parties can conduct safety audits.
relevant_disciplines: export control and national security law
on_scope_evidence: comparative safety and misuse outcomes of open-weight versus closed-weight frontier releases
which safety evaluations require weights versus black-box, log, or structured access
existing transparency instruments such as model cards, system cards, and the EU AI Act
trade-secret, copyright, and export-control treatment of model weights
documented fine-tuning, jailbreak, and misuse pathways enabled by public or leaked weights
independent audit designs including secure enclaves, NDAs, and accredited third-party evaluators
proposed or enacted disclosure statutes and executive orders aimed at frontier labs
competitive and national-security effects of a mandatory full-weight publication duty
key_tensions: independent verifiability of safety claims versus proliferation and misuse risk from publishing full weights
public-safety accountability versus trade-secret protection and competitive position of frontier labs
a legal public-publication mandate versus confidential or structured audit access that does not release weights
whether full weights are necessary for a meaningful safety audit or whether black-box and evaluation-access regimes suffice
off_scope_topics: whether frontier AI development should be paused or banned outright
training-data copyright litigation as a standalone dispute
consumer chatbot UX and product design
alignment-technique research that does not bear on audit access to weights
venture funding, startup culture, or general open-source software ideology
drift_signatures: arguing for or against AI development in general without addressing a legal duty to publish weights for audit
invoking open-source freedom or innovation benefits without linking them to independent safety-audit feasibility
debating AGI timelines, consciousness, or civilizational futures without connecting them to whether full-weight publication is required for audit
shifting to training-data copyright, labor displacement, or product UX as the decisive issue
treating internal lab safety teams or marketing transparency reports as equivalent to the independent full-weight audit the question asks about
scope.example_ceiling: Lab- and statute-level disclosure regimes, security and misuse incidents tied to released or leaked weights, and severe or national-security harm scenarios only insofar as they bear on whether public full weights are required for independent audit; unconnected extinction narratives and consumer-product anecdotes are disproportionate
scope.domain: frontier AI governance, model-weight transparency, and independent safety audit
excluded_scenarios: weight release whose purpose is commercial open-sourcing or general research access rather than independent safety audit
internal-only lab safety review as a substitute for independent audit
